stem:
In a class activity, Meera lists four things found in or near her school in Jaipur. Her teacher asks her to check two things for each: whether it has mass, and whether it occupies space. Only something that has mass AND occupies space is matter.

| thing | W | X | Y | Z |
| has mass? | yes | yes | no | yes |
| occupies space? | yes | no | yes | yes |

W = a steel tiffin box, X = the smell of agarbatti smoke, Y = the light from a tube light, Z = the water in a bottle

Which of the things are matter?

teacher.key_rationale: Matter requires both mass and occupying space. W (tiffin box) and Z (water) satisfy both conditions; X fails the occupies-space check as presented and Y fails the has-mass check (light is not matter). Therefore the answer is B (W and Z). Option A is the trap for a student who applies only the mass condition and drops the space condition.
